results.title: Why do people hate working in shipyards so much?
results.content: You get treated as a laborer not a skilled craftsman. If you take pride in your work and put good quality down, I would not recommend shipyards.

results.title: Hanwha Philly Shipyard Grapples with Further Delays After Taking Over - Shipbuilding - gCaptain Forum
results.content:
Stayed at one of North-East shipyards two years ago for a scheduled maintenance. Quite professional management on all levels. But guys who do actual work were utterly different group - one very experienced and knowledgeable dude of pre-retirement age and bunch of what looked like random people looking for a quick buck before moving on. Some didn’t even speak much English, which is fine (I am not native speaker myself) but definitely slowed down process.

Interesting article. Would not be surprised if Hanwha is using this article to start their exit strategy within the next few years. Year 1 into the Hanwha experiment, would not be surprised if this ends between Year 3 and Year 5. [...] Someone in the know may be able to confirm if SKF implemented any design changes to the bearing that is being installed for this next attempt. I suspect all of the parties (MARAD, TOTE, Hanwha) had independent firms confirm the shaft alignment like AME or DIEHL.

Hanwha has good workers, yes they are behind schedule. However difficulties happened when you can’t find good skilled labor.

Any idea how much are they paying these skilled workers?

FYI this article appears to be a cannibalized version of this: Hanwha Ocean's U.S. Training Vessel Delayed by Propulsion Defects
